summary: ECN bits stripped by customer egress appliance causing gRPC throughput degradation and long-tail streaming latency on private deploy
description: Customers on a Private deployment report intermittent long-tail latency and throughput degradation for streaming gRPC requests and large artifact downloads. Traffic traces from the customer's egress appliance show ECN (Explicit Congestion Notification) marking/ECT bits being stripped/re-written rather than preserved, causing the TCP sender in our serving nodes to fall back to conservative congestion control behavior and frequent slow-start events. The issue is most visible during large KV cache warm-ups and sharded model downloads where sustained throughput matters.
impact: FinEdge observed 95th and 99th percentile streaming latencies increase by 3–6x during busy periods; multiple user requests experienced stalls of 5–20s. Some model shard downloads reported partial content throughput degradation causing backend 503s when cache misses overlapped with reduced TCP throughput. No user data leak; availability remained degraded for affected flows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a private Redwood agent inside FinEdge VPC (prod-us-east).
2) Trigger concurrent streaming generation jobs that produce steady token output (>200 KB/s sustained per stream) across ~20 clients to simulate warm cache and shard download traffic.
3) Run tcpdump on serving node and on the customer egress appliance for the same 1-minute window capturing first SYN packets and some data packets (flags + IP TOS/ECN bits).
4) Compare ECT/CE bits on packets leaving serving node vs packets observed leaving appliance to internet.
observed_logs: tcpdump snippet (serving node): 10:41:12.345678 IP (tos 0x2,ECT(0)) 10.0.5.12.443 > 192.0.2.45.54321: Flags [P.], seq 1:1437, ack 1, win 512, length 1436
tcpdump snippet (egress appliance): 10:41:12.345789 IP (tos 0x0) 10.0.5.12.443 > 192.0.2.45.54321: Flags [P.], seq 1:1437, ack 1, win 512, length 1436
gRPC logs (serving runtime): stream stalled for 12.3s, 'transport: connection forced to close' after retransmit backoff
node metrics: cwnd reductions correlated with ECN clear events; sustained throughput dropped from 80MB/s to 7MB/s during periods where ECN cleared
kernel tcp: TCP: ECE handshake negotiation succeeded (server) followed by reset of ECT bit observed by upstream NAT
investigation_notes: 03-10 14:05: Support intake from FinEdge after they reported long-tail streaming stalls during morning ingest window.
03-10 15:20: Collected tcpdumps from both sides (customer egress appliance and serving node) and confirmed mismatch in IP TOS/ECN bits (0x2 -> 0x0).
03-11 09:10: Reproduced behaviour in lab by placing a test NAT appliance (vendor X) configured with 'ECN strip' policy; observed identical cwnd collapse and gRPC stalls.
03-11 11:00: Correlated with recent configuration push to customer's egress appliance (change request FIN-OPS-2207) that enabled an outbound inspection policy which included 'normalize TOS' behavior.
03-12 08:30: Confirmed that when ECN bits are preserved end-to-end, sender keeps larger cwnd, fewer retransmits, and streaming latency returns to baseline.
03-13 16:00: SRE validated that disabling ECN on serving nodes mitigates the tail but is not a long-term fix (reduces TCP performance overall).
workaround: Customer temporarily rolled back the 'normalize TOS' change on the egress appliance (change FIN-OPS-2207 rollback), which restored ECN preservation. As an immediate mitigation we advised FinEdge to disable ECN marking at the appliance or configure it to preserve ECT/CE bits for traffic to Redwood endpoints. On our side, we added a short-term measure to the serving runtime: detect repeated ECN clearance and extend keepalive/retry timers to avoid aggressive connection closure.
resolution_summary: Final resolution pending: customer network team will apply an appliance firmware/ACL update to preserve ECN bits for outbound flows to Redwood and other cloud endpoints. We provided a config snippet and test plan (see runbook). SRE will monitor 95/99th latency for the next 72 hours post-change. If customer cannot preserve ECN, we'll plan a controlled tuning of server-side congestion control parameters (BBR fallback / sysctl adjustments) and update the runbook.
